request.what: Reduce the committeeMinSize protocol parameter from 7 to 5.

claims.claim: The proposal changes the minimum Constitutional Committee size parameter, committeeMinSize, from 7 to 5.
The current Constitutional Committee has 7 members, equal to the current committeeMinSize setting of 7.

If committee membership drops below committeeMinSize, governance actions requiring Constitutional Committee approval become ineligible for ratification, including Parameter Changes, Constitution Updates, Treasury Withdrawals, and Hard Forks.
Reducing committeeMinSize to 5 would create an operational buffer so governance can continue if one or two members resign or their terms expire, assuming a current 7-member committee.

The proposal depends temporally on another live Parameter Change governance action for Plutus cost model settings, but the document says there is no technical interaction between the two parameter changes.
The change does not directly affect the current number of Constitutional Committee members and does not change the maximum number of members.
At a Constitutional Committee size of 5 with a 2/3 threshold, 4 constitutional votes are needed to meet threshold and 2 unconstitutional votes can prevent threshold.
The proposal states that committeeMinSize of 5 satisfies guardrails CMS-01, CMS-02, and CMS-03 because it is non-negative, not lower than 3, and not above 10.
The proposal says the change underwent technical review through the Parameter Committee Parameter Change Process and cites the Cardano Forum PCP-005 discussion.

The reversion plan says committeeMinSize can be reverted to 7 if needed, provided there are at least 7 Constitutional Committee members, but reverting while fewer than 7 members are present would immediately halt governance until enough members are elected.

summary: The document proposes a non-treasury parameter change to lower committeeMinSize from 7 to 5 to reduce governance inoperability risk, while acknowledging altered voting dynamics, temporal dependency on another parameter action, relevant guardrails, review references, and a conditional reversion plan.
